claims.claim: **No published report exists of a child acquiring a blood-borne virus from an incidental community needlestick** (hepatitis B, hepatitis C or HIV).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired needle stick injury' (Last Updated January 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_needle_stick_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Decide whether the CA-NSI is high risk, and establish the child's immunisation status.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired needle stick injury' (Last Updated January 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_needle_stick_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **History:** time, date and place · body site, superficial or deep · source known or unknown · needle/syringe type · first aid given · visible blood on or in the needle · **immunisation history, specifically tetanus and hepatitis B**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired needle stick injury' (Last Updated January 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_needle_stick_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **High-risk CA-NSI:** the source is known to carry a blood-borne virus · deliberate assault · deep, large-volume injection with a hollow-bore needle · adolescent with a personal history of injecting drug use · device visibly contaminated with blood · needle placed directly into a vein or artery.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired needle stick injury' (Last Updated January 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_needle_stick_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess and manage associated injuries first. First aid: wash the site with soap and water**, and dispose of the needle safely.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired needle stick injury' (Last Updated January 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_needle_stick_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **High-risk CA-NSI: talk to a senior clinician, and consider an Infectious Diseases referral.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired needle stick injury' (Last Updated January 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_needle_stick_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Immunised child: test hepatitis B surface antibody (HBsAb), marked urgent, with the result followed up within 72 hours** (by the ED or the GP). The anti-HBs level should be over 10 mIU/mL.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired needle stick injury' (Last Updated January 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_needle_stick_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Store serum; do not routinely test the child for hepatitis C or HIV.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired needle stick injury' (Last Updated January 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_needle_stick_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Source, if known:** test hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis C serology and HIV serology.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired needle stick injury' (Last Updated January 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_needle_stick_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Never send the syringe or needle for testing** — results on discarded injecting equipment are unreliable.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired needle stick injury' (Last Updated January 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_needle_stick_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tetanus: needlestick injuries are tetanus-prone wounds** — see `tetanus-prone-wounds`.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired needle stick injury' (Last Updated January 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_needle_stick_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hepatitis B:** follow the page's flowchart, with Australian Red Cross Lifeblood for immunoglobulin and the Immunisation Handbook for immunisation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired needle stick injury' (Last Updated January 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_needle_stick_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hepatitis C: there is no post-exposure prophylaxis for it.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired needle stick injury' (Last Updated January 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_needle_stick_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **HIV: only children with a high-risk CA-NSI are offered post-exposure prophylaxis** — discuss with Infectious Diseases.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired needle stick injury' (Last Updated January 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_needle_stick_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **PEP immunisations begin a catch-up schedule**; refer children needing further doses to their GP or local immunisation service.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired needle stick injury' (Last Updated January 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_needle_stick_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** the necessary treatment, immunisations and a plan to follow up results are arranged.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired needle stick injury' (Last Updated January 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_needle_stick_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reassure parents: viral transmission risk is exceedingly low.** Unimmunised children: give written information on hepatitis B and tetanus catch-up doses at minimum. Consider referral to the Infectious Diseases outpatient clinic.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Community acquired needle stick injury' (Last Updated January 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Community_acquired_needle_stick_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23
